answer: Recursive Cipher Custody. Each identity must hold a distinct private key whose corresponding public key is co-signed into a cedar-sealed certificate chain anchored to a hardware root of trust with a unique, non-clonable die fingerprint. Registration enforces one active chain per physical root; duplicates are rejected at issuance. An attacker must acquire and physically provision separate certified hardware per identity, and a falcon-signed challenge proves liveness of each root on every renewal.
